nodes.label: ARM Holdings
nodes.bottleneck_reason: No viable alternatives exist. Controls 95.0% market share. Critical risk level.
nodes.description: CPU/GPU architecture licensing. ARM designs power 95% of mobile processors and an increasing share of data-center and automotive chips. No viable alternative architecture exists at comparable power efficiency.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Global smartphone production halts. Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, and MediaTek lose access to the instruction set architecture powering virtually all mobile devices.

nodes.label: Cadence Design Systems
nodes.description: Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software. Together with Synopsys, forms a duopoly in chip design tools. Every advanced chip designed in the last decade used Cadence or Synopsys tools.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Chip designers lose access to verification and simulation tools. New chip designs delayed by 12-18 months as teams migrate toolchains.

nodes.label: Synopsys
nodes.description: Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software. Market leader in logic synthesis and physical verification. Part of the EDA duopoly with Cadence.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Similar to Cadence — chip design pipeline freezes. Combined with Cadence disruption, the entire semiconductor design ecosystem collapses.

nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.bottleneck_reason: No viable alternatives exist. Controls 92.0% market share. Critical risk level.
nodes.description: Advanced node fabrication. TSMC controls 92% of advanced semiconductor fabrication below 7nm. Zero substitutes exist below 5nm. Sole manufacturer of chips for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, and Qualcomm's flagship products.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Catastrophic. Apple loses A-series and M-series production. Nvidia H100/H200 production stops. AMD Ryzen and EPYC unavailable. Global AI compute capacity drops 80%+.

nodes.label: Samsung Foundry
nodes.description: Secondary advanced node fabrication. Produces chips at 3nm and 5nm but with lower yields than TSMC. Primary foundry partner for Qualcomm's mid-range chips.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Qualcomm loses secondary fab capacity. Some Google Tensor chips delayed. Limited global impact compared to TSMC disruption.

nodes.label: Intel Foundry
nodes.description: Limited advanced node capacity. Intel Foundry Services (IFS) is attempting to compete with TSMC but remains 1-2 process generations behind. Critical for US semiconductor sovereignty.
nodes.risk_if_fails: US loses domestic advanced fab capability. CHIPS Act investments at risk. National security implications for defense chip supply.

nodes.label: ASML
nodes.bottleneck_reason: No viable alternatives exist. Controls 100.0% market share. Critical risk level.
nodes.description: EUV lithography — MONOPOLY. ASML is the only company on Earth that manufactures Extreme Ultraviolet lithography machines. Without EUV, no chips below 7nm can be printed. Each machine costs $380M+ and takes 18 months to build.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Global semiconductor advancement stops. No new chips below 7nm can be manufactured. TSMC, Samsung, and Intel all depend on ASML for next-generation production.

nodes.label: Applied Materials
nodes.description: Deposition and etch equipment. Largest semiconductor equipment maker by revenue. Provides critical CVD and PVD systems used in nearly every fab worldwide.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Fab capacity expansion slows significantly. Existing fabs can maintain production but cannot upgrade or expand.

nodes.label: Lam Research
nodes.description: Etch and deposition equipment. Dominant in plasma etch systems critical for patterning advanced chips. Along with Applied Materials, forms a US-controlled equipment duopoly.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Advanced chip patterning degrades. Fabs cannot maintain precision required for sub-5nm nodes without Lam's etch tools.

nodes.label: SK Hynix
nodes.bottleneck_reason: No viable alternatives exist. Critical risk level.
nodes.description: HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) for AI chips. SK Hynix controls 53% of global HBM production and is the sole supplier of HBM3E to Nvidia for H100/H200 GPUs. HBM is the critical bottleneck for AI compute scaling.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Nvidia H100/H200 production halts. Global AI training capacity drops dramatically. No alternative HBM supplier can fill the gap within 12 months.

nodes.label: Micron
nodes.description: DRAM and NAND flash memory. Third-largest memory maker globally. Provides memory for servers, PCs, and mobile devices. Expanding into HBM to compete with SK Hynix.
nodes.risk_if_fails: DRAM supply tightens, driving up prices for servers and consumer devices. HBM diversification efforts set back.

nodes.label: Samsung Memory
nodes.description: DRAM and NAND flash memory. Largest memory manufacturer by revenue. Produces HBM but trails SK Hynix in HBM3E yields and Nvidia qualification.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Global DRAM prices spike 50-100%. Smartphone and server memory supply severely constrained. Partial impact on HBM supply.

nodes.label: ASE Group
nodes.description: Advanced packaging (OSAT). World's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test company. Provides CoWoS-like advanced packaging critical for AI chips combining logic dies with HBM.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Advanced AI chip packaging capacity drops significantly. Nvidia and Apple face 6-12 month delays on next-generation products.

nodes.label: Amkor
nodes.description: Semiconductor packaging and test. Second-largest OSAT provider. Key packaging partner for Apple and Qualcomm with facilities in South Korea and Vietnam.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Apple and Qualcomm lose secondary packaging capacity. Production shifts to ASE Group, creating bottleneck.

nodes.label: JCET
nodes.description: Semiconductor packaging. Third-largest OSAT globally. Primarily serves Chinese domestic chip companies but also packages for international clients.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Chinese domestic chip production slows. Limited global impact as alternatives exist in Taiwan and South Korea.

nodes.label: Apple
nodes.description: Designs A-series and M-series chips. Entirely dependent on TSMC for fabrication and ASE Group / Amkor for packaging.
nodes.risk_if_fails: iPhone, iPad, and Mac production stops. World's most valuable company loses its hardware revenue stream.

nodes.label: Nvidia
nodes.description: Designs H100, H200, and Blackwell AI GPUs. Entirely dependent on TSMC for fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Global AI compute expansion halts. Cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) cannot deploy new GPU capacity. AI training timelines extend by years.

nodes.label: AMD
nodes.description: Designs Ryzen CPUs and EPYC server processors, plus Instinct AI accelerators. Dependent on TSMC for all advanced fabrication.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Server CPU market loses primary Intel competitor. Data center diversification efforts stall.

nodes.label: Qualcomm
nodes.description: Designs Snapdragon mobile SoCs and 5G modems. Splits fabrication between TSMC and Samsung Foundry.
nodes.risk_if_fails: Android smartphone ecosystem loses primary chip supplier. 5G modem supply disrupted globally.

nodes.label: Intel (Chips Division)
nodes.description: Designs and manufactures x86 CPUs. Unique in being both designer and fabricator, though increasingly outsourcing to TSMC for advanced nodes.
nodes.risk_if_fails: PC and server markets lose dominant CPU supplier. x86 architecture ecosystem disrupted.

sidebar_content.title: Chip Supply Chain Dependency Graph
sidebar_content.subtitle: Supply Chain Rail · Semiconductor Layer
sidebar_content.why_this_matters: The global semiconductor supply chain is the most concentrated critical infrastructure on Earth. A single company in the Netherlands — ASML — makes the only machines capable of printing advanced chips. A single fab in Taiwan — TSMC — produces chips for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, and nearly every advanced device. This is not a market. It is a rail. And almost no one controls a redundant track.
sidebar_content.who_controls_the_rail: Three chokepoints — ASML's EUV monopoly, TSMC's fabrication dominance, and ARM's architecture licensing — mean that export controls, natural disasters, or geopolitical conflict in any one of three locations can halt global chip production.
